title: C¹ images of the regular part of a C¹ level set are countably k-rectifiable, for every y (implicit-function half of Simon Ch. 2, Thm 6.4)
statement: Let m, k, N ∈ ℕ, n := m + k, D ⊆ ℝⁿ open, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ of class C¹ on D, G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ of class C¹ (on all of ℝⁿ), and y ∈ ℝᵐ. Let S := {u ∈ ℝⁿ : DG(u) is surjective}. Then ψ(D ∩ S ∩ G⁻¹{y}) is countably k-rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable k in ℝᴺ). No assumption k > 0 or m > 0 is made. Notation: ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); DG(u) = fderiv ℝ G u; D ∩ S ∩ G⁻¹{y} means (D ∩ S) ∩ G⁻¹{y}.
lean_statement: ∀ (m k N : ℕ) (D : Set (Rn (m + k))) (ψ : Rn (m + k) → Rn N) (G : Rn (m + k) → Rn m) (y : Rn m), IsOpen D → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ D → ContDiff ℝ 1 G → CountablyRectifiable k (ψ '' (D ∩ {u | Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ G u)} ∩ G ⁻¹' {y}))
